nodes.label: Alignment constraints and binding report
nodes.rationale: Optional constraints (Xmax at rated power, buildable port, box volume cap, target F3) and the solver reports which one bound the result, so an unexpected answer is explainable.

nodes.label: Custom topology builder
nodes.rationale: Exists because the nodal formulation makes an arbitrary topology just another netlist, so anything the standard enclosure types do not cover can still be described.

nodes.label: Driver database with Thiele/Small checks
nodes.rationale: Consistency checks state what they cannot verify instead of implying a clean bill of health.

nodes.label: Enclosure and port losses (Ql)
nodes.rationale: Modelled explicitly rather than assuming a lossless box.

nodes.label: Lumped-parameter simulation
nodes.rationale: Models only the electro-mechano-acoustic circuit: no cone breakup, no directivity, no baffle diffraction. Accepted as the honest scope of every tool of this kind.

nodes.label: Projects (.wproj) and workspaces (.wsp)
nodes.rationale: Two file scopes: one design versus a whole comparison, plus automatic session restore.

nodes.label: Signal chain (EQ, crossover, room, cabin gain)
nodes.norm_label: signal chain (eq, crossover, room, cabin gain)
nodes.rationale: Passive crossover networks are evaluated against the driver's real complex load rather than a nominal resistance; in-room response uses image sources.

nodes.label: Tauri + React/TypeScript + Rust stack
nodes.rationale: Acoustics live in Rust (nalgebra, num-complex) for the numeric solve; UI in React, TypeScript, Tailwind; Tauri bridges them into a desktop app.

nodes.label: WinISD Modern
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the twenty-year-old WinISD idea with a real circuit solver instead of closed-form alignment tables, multiple drivers on shared graphs, and honest limits drawn on the model rather than left for the user to know about.

nodes.label: Cross-language pinning tests
nodes.rationale: The gate catches nothing on the day it lands - everything already passes - which is the point: it exists so that stays true. portGeometry and effectiveVas are pinned across languages because a drift between the Rust solver and its TypeScript mirror is silent by nature and would otherwise never surface.

nodes.label: Tauri system dependencies (GTK/WebKit)
nodes.rationale: Only what the crate links against is installed - the app bundle itself is not built in CI, just the library and its tests, so the full bundling toolchain is unnecessary cost.

nodes.label: Auto-alignment solver
nodes.rationale: Searches the actual circuit model for the best box and tuning rather than using classic closed-form formulas, so it works across the whole Qts range instead of only where those formulas hold. It drives the same model as the display path, so a recommendation always matches the curve shown.

nodes.label: ka = 0.5 piston-model limit
nodes.rationale: Above roughly ka = 0.5 a lumped simulation has nothing useful to say, so the graphs shade that region instead of quietly drawing a flat line through it - the limit is shown rather than left implicit.

nodes.label: Maximum SPL ceiling
nodes.rationale: Takes the lower of the excursion and thermal ceilings and marks which one is binding, rather than reporting a single unattributed number.

nodes.label: Modified nodal analysis solver
nodes.rationale: Each enclosure is built as nodes and elements (driver, chamber, port, passive radiator, radiation load) and every frequency point is one complex admittance solve. Chosen so adding an enclosure type means describing its topology rather than deriving and writing new response mathematics.

nodes.label: Transfer function normalisation
nodes.rationale: Normalised against the same driver in free air so coil, sensitivity and radiation model divide out and the curve shows what the enclosure alone contributes.
